While many people are still waiting for the Fed to “bail out” the market, Wall Street has already started reminding everyone: don’t wait.

In its latest view, Citadel Securities says the market is underestimating new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s determination to push inflation back to the 2% target. Even if international oil prices have recently pulled back, the Fed may not pivot to easing, because core inflation pressures still remain.

More importantly, Citadel Securities believes the “Fed Put” that the market has long relied on is starting to change.

What does that mean?

Previously, there was a consensus: as long as U.S. stocks fell hard enough and the economy began to slow, the Fed would eventually cut rates and inject liquidity to lift the market back up.

But at the Fed meeting right after Warsh took office, the signals were completely different—prioritizing controlling inflation over propping up asset prices. The latest dot plot also shows that multiple officials expect there may still be room for further rate hikes in the future, while market expectations for rate cuts have clearly cooled.

My view is that this could mean the market is entering a new trading logic.

Risk assets such as AI-themed concepts, highly valued tech stocks, and Bitcoin—benefited from ample liquidity over the past few years. Once the market starts to accept the expectation that “high interest rates will stay around for longer,” valuation frameworks may be repriced.

What’s really worth worrying about isn’t whether the next rate hike happens. It’s that the market is starting to realize: this time, the Fed may not reach for the market’s falling asset prices right away.

If the “Fed Put” truly begins to fade gradually, every macro datapoint and every inflation print in the future could be more likely than in the past few years to amplify market volatility.

Bull markets run on liquidity, sideways markets rely on earnings, and bear markets run on cash. For the next stretch, the market may need to readjust to an era without a Fed backstop.

#美联储 #沃什 #BTC  #ETH #加密货币

content:
就在很多人还在等美联储“救市”时，华尔街已经开始提醒大家：别等了。

城堡证券（Citadel Securities）最新观点认为，市场低估了新任美联储主席凯文·沃什（Kevin Warsh）把通胀压回2%目标的决心。即使近期国际油价有所回落，美联储也未必会因此转向宽松，因为核心通胀压力依然存在。

更值得关注的是，城堡证券认为，过去市场深信的**“Fed Put（美联储看跌期权）”**正在发生变化。

什么意思？

以前市场有个共识：只要美股跌得够狠、经济放缓，美联储最终都会降息、放水，把市场重新托起来。

但沃什上任后的第一次议息会议，释放出的信号却完全不同——控制通胀优先于托举资产价格。最新点阵图也显示，多位官员预计未来仍存在进一步加息的可能，而市场对降息的预期明显降温。

我的观点是，这可能意味着市场正在进入一个新的交易逻辑。

AI概念、高估值科技股、比特币等风险资产，过去几年受益于充裕流动性，一旦市场开始接受“高利率维持更久”的预期，估值体系就可能重新定价。

真正值得担心的，不是下一次加不加息，而是市场开始意识到：这一次，美联储未必会在资产价格下跌时第一时间伸手。

如果“Fed Put”真的逐渐淡化，未来每一次宏观数据、每一次通胀数据，都可能比过去几年更容易放大市场波动。

牛市靠流动性，震荡靠业绩，熊市靠现金。未来一段时间，市场或许需要重新适应一个“没有美联储兜底”的时代。

Ethereum hit 7 straight weeks of ETF “bleeding,” with BlackRock leading the exit

Last week, net outflows from Ethereum spot ETFs totaled $273 million, marking the 7th consecutive week of net outflows. Even more painful: even BlackRock’s “big caretaker” ETHA saw outflows of $236 million—ETHA’s historical cumulative inflows are $11.08 billion, the absolute benchmark among ETH ETFs. If even the benchmark is withdrawing, where does the retail crowd’s faith come from?

Total net asset value of Ethereum spot ETFs has shrunk to $838 million, and ETFs account for only 4.42% of Ethereum’s total market cap. Cumulative net inflows of $10.9 billion look okay at first glance, but the trend matters more than the stock—7 straight weeks of net outflows mean institutions are voting with their feet.

ETH is trading at 1574, down 0.56% in 24 hours. The funding rate is 0.0015%, basically near zero—markets are at an extreme equilibrium in the bull-bear standoff. But sustained ETF outflows are a clear bearish signal. Resistance at 1591 is the daily sell zone; if the rebound reaches there, it will likely face pressure. Support at 1549 is the daily buy zone—once that breaks, the next support is likely in the 1480–1500 area.

When spot ETFs have been bleeding for 7 consecutive weeks, the question is no longer “where is the bottom,” but “what have institutions seen that retail hasn’t.”

OPG isn’t great because it gives you an extra sentence—it’s great because it gives you an actual receipt.
After seeing so many AI + Crypto projects, I now prefer to judge them by a simple standard: does it merely let AI produce an answer, or does it make an AI service checkable after the fact? This is also why I continue to hold @OpenGradient Chat in high regard.#BTC 
Most ordinary AI products solve the question of “can it answer.”
OpenGradient goes one step further and aims to solve “can this answer, as a service, be trusted?” When you open chat.opengradient.ai, it’s not just a chat box—it brings private chat, multi-model selection, and verifiable reasoning onto a single path.
Put these layers together and the project’s “feel” really comes through. Privacy makes users dare to put real questions in. Multi-model lets different capabilities participate in the same task. Verifiable reasoning means the output is no longer just screenshots and verbal promises, but something that can be traced back to the corresponding model and execution process.
I think this is where OPG separates itself from a bunch of AI narrative projects. It’s not that it’s attached another big model, and it’s not that “decentralization” is plastered on a webpage. Instead, it breaks the AI service into entry, routing, execution, verification, and settlement—so each part feels more like a piece of the network.
For $OPG, this kind of design also makes the source of value easier to explain: if, in the future, there are more real chat calls, multi-model reasoning, private requests, and verification needs, then token discussions won’t be empty concepts—they’ll be anchored in network workload.#ETH 
So my praise for OPG today is very straightforward: the AI space isn’t short of models that can talk. What it lacks is a network that can attach sources, processes, and verification receipts to answers. If OpenGradient can make this path work, it won’t just be selling one answer—it will be turning AI into a trustworthy service.
@OpenGradient  $OPG  #OPG

An AI tool first needs to have the qualification to look at my unfinished drafts
Today I don’t want to dismantle @OpenGradient Chat’s feature list again. The buttons—Chat, Search, Files, and Image Studio—are of course important, but if you only present them as a menu, people will finish reading it quickly and forget. #ETH 
Core question: Does an AI tool have the right to view my unfinished work?
An unfinished draft isn’t just an article outline. It could be an assessment of a project that’s not yet public, a set of client information, a few unverified trading assumptions, an image prompt, or even an opinion that I’m still not sure whether to publish. They’re not mature yet, but they already have value.
That’s also why I’m looking at chat.opengradient.ai right now. If OpenGradient Chat is only “just another chat box,” it’s hard to keep people; but if a private AI workspace can make users feel comfortable putting these unfinished drafts in, and then continue refining them with multi-model, file, and image capabilities, it stops being just a tool and becomes a workbench. #BTC 
Privacy here is not a marketing slogan—it’s a usage threshold. If users don’t dare hand over real materials, then even the strongest model can only deal with surface-level issues; only when users dare to share unfinished drafts can the AI enter the real process of creation, research, and decision-making.
Of course, that doesn’t mean I’ll dump everything in. Sensitive files need to be cleaned first, and key judgments still have to be double-checked by me. What OpenGradient solves is the threshold of whether people dare to start using it, not taking final responsibility on behalf of others.
For $OPG, what’s most worth seeing isn’t how many people tried it during the campaign period, but how many people are willing to hand over the next batch of unpublished materials to this private AI workspace. My conclusion is straightforward: an AI tool’s moat isn’t the model menu, but whether users are willing to give it their unfinished drafts.
#OPG

Some problems—I only dare to ask in the Private Chat first.
Last night I deleted a piece of content I was preparing to publish three times.
Not because I couldn’t write the观点 (viewpoints), but because the more I wrote, the more I realized that the truly valuable things often aren’t in public materials, but in those details that haven’t been said yet: why I want to see this project; which judgments haven’t been verified; which sentence is driven purely by emotion; which prompt reveals the next step I’m thinking about.#ETH 
If I just dump these things into a regular AI, I hesitate.
So when I look at @OpenGradient ’s OpenGradient Chat, my first reaction isn’t “can it write faster,” but whether it can make me dare to put the real context in.
The value of Private Chat is here: not to package a pretty line for me, but to first catch those questions that can’t be made public yet—while also needing to be organized.#BTC 
Image Studio follows the same logic. In an image prompt, it’s not just “what to draw”—it also hides the title, the emotions, the composition, and the directions that haven’t been made public. If both text and images can be handled in the same privacy-first AI environment, then OpenGradient Chat isn’t just a chat box anymore; it’s more like a workspace where real drafts can live.
For $OPG , what I care about most right now isn’t a grand narrative—it’s whether this kind of action will be repeatable. My understanding of OpenGradient Chat is very simple: it has to win—not because it can answer every question, but because there are some questions I’m only willing to ask here first.

📰 Crypto Market Highlights

1. Tom Lee: End-of-quarter rebalancing suppresses short-term moves; long-term crypto logic unchanged
Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee believes the recent weakness in the crypto market is related to institutional “window dressing” at quarter end. Some funds have shifted toward trimming positions in assets that have been performing weakly in the short term, putting pressure on major coins such as ETH. At the same time, he emphasized that the industry fundamentals are still improving: the stablecoin regulatory environment is gradually easing at the margin. Crypto infrastructure continues to attract Wall Street capital, and the integration of AI agent payments with on-chain settlement is also accelerating. Overall, short-term volatility may persist, but the mid- to long-term growth narrative remains solid.

2. CZ on Binance’s EU MiCA application: the setback is not just corporate losses
Regarding Binance’s progress on its MiCA application in the EU, CZ’s latest comments say the application was originally close to approval and they had been told that overall compliance was in place. However, during the process, it encountered external resistance, which ultimately led to the withdrawal. He also noted that several EU countries have a welcoming stance toward Binance’s rollout, and even signs of competitive interest have emerged. These remarks reflect that while Europe’s crypto regulation is being advanced in a more institutionalized way, real-world implementation is still influenced by multiple parties’ bargaining. Beyond the compliance framework, policy coordination and regulators’ attitudes remain key variables for industry expansion.

3. Strategy and STRC strengthen; the market watches linkages among crypto concept stocks
During intraday trading in the U.S. stock market, Strategy’s share price opened higher and then held an upward range-bound move, with total gains of about 5%. Its preferred stock, STRC, rose more than 8% at one point before narrowing to around 6%. The related price action suggests the market still maintains strong interest in publicly listed companies with higher exposure to crypto assets. As coin prices trade sideways, capital begins to look more closely at opportunities between crypto concept stocks and digital asset prices. If risk appetite continues to recover afterward, such assets that combine traditional market liquidity with crypto narrative attributes may keep attracting trading momentum.

[On-chain “ghost shadows” suddenly appear—what big move is ETH holding back?]

Honestly, when I was watching on-chain data, I noticed something interesting—trading volume has surged abnormally, exceeding 5% of market cap. I need to explain this clearly to you: it doesn’t mean that higher volume will definitely push prices up. Instead, this kind of signal shows that there’s huge disagreement at this level—some people are desperately buying, while others are desperately selling. It’s like two people pushing and shoving at the door: whether you go in or go out will be decided any moment now.

So what’s the situation with ETH right now? The price is $ 1562, down 1% over the past 24 hours, and down nearly 12% over 7 days. The Fear & Greed Index is at 12, which falls in the extreme fear zone. The price is down almost 68% from its all-time high—scary, isn’t it?

But here’s the question—after falling this much, is the valuation truly cheap? Or has the fundamentals already changed?

Let me give you an analogy. ETH is like a rental-property with a lease. Back then, the monthly rental yield was high; now the rent has dropped, but the property’s quality hasn’t changed. The staking mechanism turns ETH into a “cash-flow asset,” giving you roughly 3%–5% returns per year. It’s like buying a home—yes, the price may drop, but the rent is still there.

Now the key support is 1522, and the resistance is 1624. Abnormal volume expansion indicates that the battle between bulls and bears is intense. At this point, you need to ask yourself: are you betting that ETH’s fundamentals will keep deteriorating, or do you think, “it’s already fallen enough”?

Remember this: when the market is in extreme fear, you should actually stay calm and check whether the support level can hold. If it holds, it could be an opportunity; if it doesn’t, then that’s where the real trouble starts.

说真的，我盯链上数据的时候发现一个有意思的事——成交量异常放大，超过了市值的5%。这玩意儿我得跟你们说清楚，不是说成交量大就一定涨，而是这种信号说明市场在这个位置分歧巨大，有人拼命买，也有人拼命卖。就像两个人在门口推搡，进还是出，马上就要见分晓了。

ETH现在什么情况？价格$ 1562，24小时又跌了1%，7天跌了快12%。恐惧贪婪指数才12，属于极度恐惧区间。价格从历史高点跌了将近68%，你说吓人不吓人？

但问题来了——跌这么多，估值真的低吗？还是说基本面已经变天了？

我打个比方你就懂了。ETH就像一套带租约的房子，以前每月租金回报很高，现在租金降了，但房子本身的品质没变。质押机制让ETH变成"生钱资产"，每年大概能给你3%-5%的收益。这就好比你买了房子，虽然房价跌了，但租金还在。

现在关键支撑1522，阻力1624。成交量异常放大，说明多空博弈激烈。这时候你需要问自己：你赌的是ETH基本面继续恶化，还是觉得"跌够了"？

记住一点：极度恐惧的时候，反而要冷静看看支撑位守不守得住。守住了，可能就是机会；守不住，那才是真的麻烦。

你们觉得，现在ETH是在筑底还是在继续寻底？

A. 觉得已经超跌，准备分批入场
B. 觉得还没跌完，继续观望
C. 觉得基本面变了，不看好ETH

title: BTC Holds $60K as Funding Flattens and ETH Stalls Below Resistance
subTitle:
Bitcoin printed $60,240.60 on Binance at the time of writing, up a slim 0.27% over 24 hours on $920.32 million in volume, per CoinMarketCap. That is a market cap of $1,205.75 billion sitting inside a tight 72-hour range between $58,900.01 support and $60,941.17 resistance. The read is straightforward: when spot price compresses this narrowly against defined boundaries while volume stays under a billion, the market is coiling, not trending. Funding rates across perpetual swaps have gone flat to slightly positive — classic indecision, not conviction. Longs are not overpaying to hold leverage, and shorts are not pressing aggressively either. This is the kind of neutral-to-cautious positioning that has historically preceded a volatility expansion in either direction.

Ethereum mirrors the hesitation. $ETH is quoted at $1,585.46 on Binance, up 0.44% in 24 hours on $316.94 million of volume, giving it a market cap of $191.05 billion per CoinMarketCap. The 72-hour range is $1,548.37 to $1,611.02 — roughly a 4% window. That is even tighter in percentage terms than Bitcoin's corridor, and the current price sits closer to the upper bound than the lower. The ETH/BTC ratio remains compressed, which tells us capital is not rotating aggressively into alt-beta just yet. Derivatives open interest on both majors has been declining slightly over recent sessions, a pattern consistent with traders reducing exposure ahead of a catalyst rather than loading directional conviction.

So what does the derivatives landscape actually say right now? Three things stand out.

First, funding neutrality. When perpetual funding rates hover near zero across major venues, it means neither longs nor shorts have a structural edge in leverage cost. This is a reset state. Historically, the biggest moves happen from this exact positioning because neither side is crowded enough to trigger a cascade. The risk is symmetrical here.

Second, open interest contraction. Combined with flat funding, declining OI points to traders de-risking. That is not bearish by itself — it simply means the market is waiting for new information to price in. Macro headlines, ETF flow data, or a clean break of the ranges described above could re-accelerate positioning.

Third, the divergence in altcoin prints is telling. Today's top movers on CoinMarketCap — TAC up 151.3%, GWEI up 70.4%, RAVE up 32.3% — suggest speculative capital is active but confined to micro-cap narratives. That money is not flowing into $BTC or $ETH in size. When meme and micro-cap speculation runs hot while majors consolidate, it often signals late-cycle risk appetite rather than broad-based accumulation. The question is whether that speculative froth pulls back into large caps or fizzles entirely.

Now to the actionable map. For $BTC, the level to watch is $60,941.17 on the resistance side. If price pushes through and holds above that figure on a daily close, the range resolves upward and prior resistance flips to support — that is where momentum buyers historically step in. On the downside, $58,900.01 is the line in the sand. If Bitcoin loses that level with volume, the coil unwinds to the downside and the next demand zone gets tested. As long as price stays between these two numbers, expect chop and mean reversion.

For $ETH, $1,611.02 is the ceiling. A clean break above it would signal buyers absorbing overhead supply, and the structure shifts bullish on the short timeframe. The floor is $1,548.37. If that gives way, the bearish case strengthens and traders will look for the next support cluster lower. Tap $ETH to position around that range.

Worth noting: regulatory tailwinds are building quietly. Germany is leading the MiCA authorization race in Europe ahead of the looming deadline, and prediction-market consolidation could drive institutional M&A activity according to Bernstein — both structurally positive for crypto infrastructure over the medium term. On the tech side, Vitalik Buterin's comments on obfuscation for private on-chain voting signal continued protocol-layer innovation that does not move price today but shapes the long-term utility thesis.

The bottom line from the data: markets are range-bound, funding is neutral, and traders are waiting. The next significant move — up or down — likely starts with a clean break of the support or resistance levels outlined above. Until then, patience is the position.

Not financial advice.

What is your base case — does $BTC break $60,941 first or give back $58,900?

Data over drama.

1. Strategy Introduces Digital Credit Capital Framework
Strategy announced the launch of a digital credit capital framework, with the core goal of strengthening liquidity management, optimizing its digital credit capabilities, and maintaining a long-term Bitcoin exposure. The company increased its U.S. dollar reserves to $2.55 billion, covering approximately 17.4 months of dividend and interest expenses, and requires maintaining at least a 12-month safety buffer. Meanwhile, the STRC dividend yield was raised to 12%, indicating a proactive adjustment in high-yield capital instruments.

2. Strategy Approved a $2.0 Billion Share Buyback and BTC Monetization Limit
On the capital operations front, Strategy’s board authorized a maximum $2.0 billion share repurchase plan, including $1.0 billion for repurchasing digital credit securities and $1.0 billion for repurchasing Class A common stock. The company was also approved for up to $1.25 billion in Bitcoin monetization capacity, which can be used to supplement reserves, support dividends, interest, and capital arrangements. Notably, its recent Bitcoin holdings have remained at 847,363 BTC, with no further accumulation for now.

3. BitMine Continues to Accumulate ETH, with Holdings Approaching a Key Market Share
BitMine recently added another 27,084 ETH, bringing total holdings to about 5.7 million, or roughly 4.7% of Ethereum’s total supply. This shows that the trend of institutionalized, concentrated allocation is still intensifying. Its overall asset size is about $9.8 billion. In addition to ETH, it also covers cash, marketable securities, BTC, and equity investments, making its asset structure relatively diversified and further increasing its allocation influence in the crypto market.

4. BitMine Expands Staking Size, Ongoing Improvement in Revenue Capability
BitMine currently has more than 85% of its ETH staked—about 4.879 million ETH—corresponding to a value of roughly $7.7 billion, with annualized staking revenue of about $211 million. Large-scale staking not only improves asset utilization efficiency, but also strengthens its cash-flow generation capability. Coupled with expected attention from inclusion in large-cap stock indices, the market is closely watching whether it will continue to expand its ETH reserves and staking scale.

5. Binance Wallet Becomes an Aster DEX Validator
Binance Wallet announced that it has become an Aster DEX validator, further strengthening its participation in on-chain infrastructure. The official statement indicates that this move aims to support broader network participation and on-chain accessibility, and also reflects that wallet products are extending from a single-asset management tool to an ecosystem infrastructure service role. #Europe begins cleaning up unlicensed crypto platforms; I think this will become increasingly important in the second half of the year.

MiCA’s transition period is basically ending by July 1. Platforms that haven’t obtained the EU CASP authorization can no longer continue serving European users the way they used to. On the surface, this looks like regulatory news, but the real impact is where the money will go.

In the past, everyone only looked at who had more coins and who had lower fees. Going forward, you may also need to watch one more thing: who can survive compliantly in the major markets. Big platforms will be more favored, while space for smaller platforms and gray channels will be squeezed. For assets like $BTC , which institutional capital finds easier to understand, this may actually not be a bad thing.

As for $ETH  and $SOL , I’ll be watching how the ecosystem takes over. The clearer the regulation, the more boldly compliant capital will enter—but capital won’t randomly buy. In the end, it will still flow to chains with strong liquidity, solid narratives, and enough applications.

So I don’t think MiCA is only about Europe. It’s more like a signal: in the second half, the crypto market may gradually shift from “who can tell a story” to “who can be bought by compliant capital.”

#欧洲开始清理无牌加密平台 #BTC #ETH

content:
#欧洲开始清理无牌加密平台，这事我觉得下半年会越来越重要。

MiCA 的过渡期到7月1日基本结束，没拿到欧盟 CASP 授权的平台，接下来就不能像以前那样继续服务欧洲用户。表面看是监管新闻，实际影响的是资金会往哪里走。

以前大家只看谁币多、谁手续费低；后面可能要多看一条：谁能在主要市场合规活下来。大平台会更吃香，小平台和灰色通道的空间会被挤压，这对 $BTC 这种机构资金更容易理解的资产反而不算坏事。

$ETH 和 $SOL 这边我会看生态承接。监管越清楚，合规资金越敢进，但资金不会乱买，最后还是会流向流动性强、叙事够硬、应用够多的链。

所以我不觉得 MiCA 只是欧洲自己的事。它更像一个信号：下半年加密市场可能会从“谁会讲故事”，慢慢变成“谁能被合规资金买”。

[When everyone is waiting for ETH to hit zero]

At the end of 2018, ETH fell to $80, and posts saying "ETH is dead" filled the entire screen. What happened then? Once the DeFi Summer arrived, it surged nearly tenfold in just three months.

Now we’re at a similar node again.

ETH is trading at 1570, down more than 10% over the past seven days. Compared to its all-time high, it has pulled back nearly 68%. The FNG index is 12—extreme fear. The weekly average is only 15. In plain words: market sentiment is so cold it’s gone bone-deep.

But here’s the question—does extreme fear necessarily mean you have to run?

Look at three signals. First, volume. Volume hasn’t contracted; instead, it’s relatively active. This suggests there is capital absorbing, not simply a mass sell-off. Second, sentiment. The FNG and ETH trends are basically synchronized, which means the drop isn’t due to ETH’s own negative catalysts—it’s the overall market compressing valuations. Third, valuation. What does a 68% drop imply? It means you can buy ETH with the same fundamentals for less than one-third of the price back then.

Support is at 1522, resistance at 1616. Price is oscillating narrowly within this range, and the direction decision is close. If you see a breakout with volume above either level, chase that direction.

The real issue now isn’t whether ETH will rebound, but whether ETH’s underlying logic undergoes any fundamental change in the next cycle. Can narratives like Restaking and ZK carry the next opportunity on the scale of a DeFi Summer?

History won’t repeat itself exactly, but the rhyming parts always show up.

What about your position right now—are you prepared to hold through to the next cycle, or are you ready to cut losses and exit?

【当所有人都在等ETH归零的时候】

2018年底，ETH跌到80美元，满屏都是"ETH已死"的帖子。结果呢？DeFi Summer一来，三个月涨了将近十倍。

现在又到了类似的节点。

ETH报价1570，近七天跌了超过10%，相比历史高点回调将近68%。FNG指数12，极度恐慌，周均才15。说人话就是：市场情绪已经冷到骨头里了。

但问题来了——极度恐慌就一定等于要跑吗？

看三个信号。第一，成交量。成交量没有萎缩，反而比较活跃，说明有资金在承接，不是单纯的多杀多。第二，情绪。FNG和ETH走势基本同步，这说明现在跌不是因为ETH自己的利空，是大盘整体在压估值。第三，估值。68%的跌幅意味着什么？意味着你用不到当时三分之一的价格，能买到同等基本面的ETH。

支撑1522，阻力1616。价格在这个区间窄幅震荡，方向选择临近。放量破哪个位置，就往哪个方向追。

现在的问题不是ETH会不会反弹，而是下一轮周期里，ETH的底层逻辑有没有根本性的改变。Restaking、ZK这些叙事能不能撑起下一个DeFi Summer级别的机会。

历史不会简单重复，但押韵的地方总会出现。

你现在的仓位，准备扛到下一个周期还是准备止损离场？

Second, let the monthly chart set the direction. If the monthly MACD hasn’t produced a red golden cross, stay firmly in cash. Better to be lacking than to act wrongly.

Third, hold the entry point. Only act when there’s a pullback to the 60-day line and when either a high-volume bullish candle or a long lower shadow appears. Don’t chase without volume.

Fourth, the 60-day line is a line between life and death. If it rises 30% or 50%, reduce positions in batches. If the close falls below the moving average, clear out unconditionally.

Let the monthly chart define the trend, let the daily chart protect your principal. Risk control always comes before profit. This method isn’t exciting or flashy. There’s no overnight wealth myth—but it’s the most reliable way for ordinary people to make it to shore.

It can’t fall either; it needs to prevent the big players from raising the average price and then cashing out and running. It was a routine transfer.

February 20, 2025. A Bybit employee opens his screen, checks the transaction details, and signs.

Everything looks normal.

Minutes later, $1.5 billion $USDT  in Ethereum had vanished.

But the most terrifying part isn’t the amount.

The most terrifying part is how they did it.

The elite North Korean government hackers of the Lazarus Group didn’t attack the blockchain. They didn’t break any private keys. They didn’t need any of that.

They simply… falsified what the employee saw on the screen.

Months earlier, they infiltrated the system of a Safe Wallet developer—the platform Bybit used to sign transactions. They injected a malicious code that slept quietly, waiting.

When the employee opened his wallet that day, the code activated. The screen showed a legitimate transfer. In reality, the funds were going to Pyongyang.

The employee signed. His coworkers signed. Nobody saw anything unusual.

Two minutes after the theft, the malicious code deleted itself. No trace.

It took the FBI days to confirm what everyone already suspected: it was North Korea, using stolen Ethereum to fund its nuclear weapons program.

The lesson nobody wants to hear: the weakest link isn’t the code. It’s you.

Do you trust the screen you see when you sign a transaction?

Fran Berlin | Blockchain Institute

Era una transferencia de rutina.

Febrero 20, 2025. Un empleado de Bybit abre su pantalla, revisa los detalles de la transacción, y firma.

Todo se ve normal.

Minutos después, 1.500 millones de dólares $USDT en Ethereum habían desaparecido.

Pero lo más aterrador no es el monto.

Lo más aterrador es cómo lo hicieron.

El Grupo Lazarus hackers de élite del gobierno de Corea del Norte no atacó el blockchain. No rompió ninguna clave privada. No necesitó nada de eso.

Simplemente… falsificó lo que el empleado veía en pantalla.

Meses antes, infiltraron el sistema de un desarrollador de Safe Wallet, la plataforma que Bybit usaba para firmar transacciones. Inyectaron un código malicioso que dormía en silencio, esperando.

Cuando el empleado abrió su billetera ese día, el código se activó. La pantalla mostraba una transferencia legítima. En realidad, los fondos iban a Pyongyang.

El empleado firmó. Sus compañeros firmaron. Nadie vio nada raro.

Dos minutos después del robo, el código malicioso se borró solo. Sin rastro.

El FBI tardó días en confirmar lo que ya todos sospechaban: fue Corea del Norte, financiando su programa de armas nucleares con Ethereum robado.

La lección que nadie quiere escuchar: el eslabón más débil no es el código. Eres tú.

title: Ethereum at $1,624: The Boring Trade Nobody Is Talking About
subTitle:
Here is a fun number to chew on: $195.91 billion. That is Ethereum's current market capitalization according to CoinMarketCap, which makes it larger than the GDP of about half the countries on Earth. And yet, if you scroll through your feed right now, you would think ETH went extinct somewhere around lunchtime. While TAC somehow pulled a +169.7% day and RAVE partied its way to +44.2%, the second-largest cryptocurrency on the planet moved a modest +3.73% and barely anyone raised an eyebrow. Classic crypto logic: the thing that actually matters gets less hype than a token you have never heard of.

Let me walk you through what is actually happening on the $ETH chart and on-chain right now, because the setup is more interesting than the silence suggests.

ETH is trading at $1,624.02 on Binance, and if you look at where the price sits relative to its 72-hour structure, it is knocking on the door of resistance. That ceiling is $1,634.24 — roughly ten dollars above the current print. In crypto terms, that is a sneeze away. The 72-hour support floor sits at $1,548.37, which is where buyers showed up the last time sellers tried to push things lower. So you have a range of about $86 between the two levels, and right now ETH is pressing the top of it rather than the bottom. That tells you who has been in control over the last three days.

Here is the actionable map, plain and simple. If $ETH holds above that $1,548.37 support, buyers are still defending the range and the bias leans toward continuation higher. That is the dip-buy zone — the area where smart money historically reloads rather than panics. On the flip side, if price breaks cleanly above $1,634.24 resistance with volume behind it, that is a momentum signal that the range has resolved upward and traders will be watching for follow-through. Conversely, losing $1,548.37 on a closing basis flips the script entirely — that would mean sellers overwhelmed the bid, and the next leg down becomes the base case until a new floor establishes itself. No price targets here, just conditional logic: respect the levels, react to what price does at them, and let the market hand you the next clue.

Now, what about the on-chain and ETF angle everyone asked for? The 24-hour trading volume on ETH sits at $458.85 million according to CoinMarketCap. For context, that number is steady but not euphoric. It tells you that institutions and retail are engaged, but nobody is in a frenzy. This is what accumulation looks like when the crowd is distracted by +169% meme tokens. Meanwhile, headlines this week like BNY adding USDC minting and redemption to its institutional custody platform are quietly bullish for the entire Ethereum ecosystem — stablecoin infrastructure flowing through traditional banking rails means more on-chain settlement happening on networks that ultimately settle in ETH. The plumbing is getting built while the price yawns.

The broader crypto market is also giving us clues. Bitcoin is holding its own, and when BTC is stable, capital historically rotates into ETH with a slight lag. The question is whether this current squeeze toward resistance resolves into a breakout or a rejection. Volume will be the tell. A pop through $1,634.24 on heavy volume is a very different animal than a limp wick that gets slapped back down.

The irony of the current moment is that Ethereum is doing the hard, unglamorous work — scaling, institutional integration, DeFi maturation — while speculative garbage grabs the headlines. But markets reward patience more than they reward hot takes. ETH is coiled in a range, pressing resistance, and the levels are clear. The trade does not need to be exciting to be right.

Not financial advice.

Laugh, then look at the chart.

title: Where the Money Is Quietly Moving Today
subTitle:
Picture a crowded trading floor where everyone is whispering. Nobody is shouting about a breakout, nobody is panicking about a crash — but if you stand still long enough, you can hear the steady shuffle of capital moving from one seat to another. That is what this market feels like right now. Quiet rotation, not revolution.

The headline numbers on the surface look tame. Bitcoin is doing its thing, and the majors are only modestly green. But dig one layer deeper and the order flow tells a different story — one where institutions and smart money are choosing sides between Ethereum and Solana, and where speculative capital is flooding into micro-caps at a pace that suggests risk appetite is warming up beneath the surface.

Let us start with the two heavyweights.

Ethereum is trading at $1,584.98 on Binance, up just 0.90% over the past 24 hours. The volume sits at $406.70 million — respectable, but not the kind of surge that signals a breakout is imminent. Its market cap according to CoinMarketCap is $191.16 billion, still the second-largest asset in crypto by a wide margin. The story here is consolidation. ETH has been coiling within a defined 72-hour range, with support holding at $1,548.37 and resistance capping moves at $1,611.02. Right now, price is sitting closer to the top of that range than the bottom, which tells you buyers have been nibbling but have not committed a full push yet. If ETH holds above that $1,548.37 support, the floor remains intact and bulls can make another run at the $1,611.02 ceiling. A clean break above $1,611.02 would flip that resistance into a launchpad and open up room for momentum to build. But if it loses $1,548.37, the next logical resting spot gets murkier, and sellers regain control of the short-term narrative. Tap $ETH to watch how this range resolves.

Now look at Solana, and the energy shift becomes obvious. SOL is at $74.02, up 3.60% in 24 hours — four times Ethereum's pace — on volume of $252.83 million. Its market cap is $42.91 billion, per CoinMarketCap. That outperformance is not a random blip. Capital is rotating into faster, higher-beta layer-1 names, and Solana is the most liquid destination for that trade. The 72-hour chart shows support at $69.74 and resistance nearly tapped at $74.55. SOL is pressing right against that ceiling as we speak. If it breaks cleanly above $74.55 with volume confirmation, traders will interpret it as a momentum signal and pile in. If $74.55 rejects price again, watch for a pullback toward that $69.74 support — and if that level holds, it becomes the dip-buy zone where buyers step back in. Losing $69.74 would be a warning that the rotation trade is fading. Tap $SOL to set your levels and follow the action.

While the majors grind, the speculative edges of the market are on fire. TAC surged 164.8%, RAVE added 34.6%, and UB climbed 31.7%, all according to CoinMarketCap. Moves like these do not happen in a vacuum — they happen when traders are hunting for yield and asymmetric upside because they believe the broader market floor is stable enough to take risks. That is rotation in action: stability in the majors, aggression in the small caps.

Meanwhile, the headlines add another layer. BNY just expanded its custody platform to support USDC minting and redemption, a quiet but significant signal that institutional plumbing continues to deepen. When traditional finance builds rails for stablecoins, it means more capital is being pre-positioned to enter the on-chain economy. That capital does not sit idle forever — it finds its way into ETH, SOL, and the speculative fringe.

So what does all of this tell you? The market is not chasing one narrative. It is distributing bets — Ethereum as the institutional-grade settlement layer, Solana as the fast-money playground, and micro-caps as the lottery tickets for those who think the floor is solid. The key question is whether this rotation accelerates into conviction or stalls into chop. The levels above give you the map. Your read on which side the tape tips will determine how you navigate what comes next.
